what.text: Klotho is a protein made by the body. It was named in 1997, when researchers found that mice lacking the klotho gene developed a syndrome that looked like early ageing: a short life, infertility, hardened arteries, thin skin, bone loss and emphysema. The gene makes a protein that sits in the cell membrane and resembles beta-glucosidase enzymes.
A form of klotho also circulates in the blood. A 2005 mouse study described it as a hormone that dampens insulin and IGF-1 signalling inside cells.
How it acts, according to animal and cell studies:

items.text: Mice engineered to make extra klotho lived longer than normal mice.
Mice engineered to make extra klotho did better on learning and memory tests, and showed stronger connections between brain cells.
A single injection of klotho protein under the skin improved memory tests in old rhesus monkeys, at a low dose but not at higher doses.

what.text: None of these effects has been tested by giving klotho protein to people.

research.text: Human evidence: no published study has given klotho protein to people. Human data link blood levels or gene variants with health. Two small gene-therapy pilots that inject klotho DNA are registered and have posted no results.

The searches found no published study and no registered trial in which klotho protein itself was given to people. The registry lists two pilot studies of klotho gene therapy (below). A 2020 study measured klotho in the cord blood of preterm babies, but gave klotho only to rat pups.

research.title: Blood klotho and death in older adults (InCHIANTI)

facts.v: Semba RD, et al. J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci 2011;66(7):794-800
observational; no one was given klotho
804 adults aged 65 or older in Tuscany
6 years of follow-up
plasma klotho and death from any cause

research.found: 194 people (24.1%) died. After adjusting for age, sex, diseases and other factors, people in the lowest third of klotho levels had a higher risk of death than those in the highest third (hazard ratio 1.78). The authors say more studies are needed to find out why. An association like this cannot show that klotho causes longer life.

src.label: Semba et al., J Gerontol A, 2011

research.title: A klotho gene variant and thinking skills

facts.v: Dubal DB, et al. Cell Rep 2014;7(4):1065-76
genetic association in people, plus mouse experiments. No person was given klotho.
the KL-VS variant of the klotho gene, blood klotho levels and cognitive test scores

research.found: People with one copy of KL-VS had better cognitive scores and higher blood klotho. The abstract does not give the number of people.

research.title: Klotho plasmid gene therapy in healthy adults

facts.v: NCT07216781, sponsored by Minicircle
single group, open-label, no placebo
14 healthy adults aged 23 to 90 enrolled
klotho DNA in a non-viral plasmid, injected under the skin into belly fat
blood klotho, side effects, FGF23, parathyroid hormone, vitamin D, phosphate, cognitive tests
The registry says the product is given at a clinic in Roatán, Honduras, outside FDA jurisdiction; only before-and-after testing takes place at a US site in Austin, Texas.

research.found: Started October 2025. Active, not recruiting. No results posted. This is gene therapy, not klotho protein.

research.title: Klotho plus follistatin gene therapy

facts.v: NCT07285629, sponsored by Minicircle
single group, open-label, no placebo
14 healthy adults aged 50 to 80 enrolled
klotho and follistatin DNA in a non-viral plasmid, injected into belly fat
blood klotho and follistatin, side effects, for 3 months

research.found: Listed as completed in April 2026. No results posted.

research.title: One klotho injection and memory in old rhesus monkeys

facts.v: Castner SA, et al. Nat Aging 2023;3(8):931-7
monkeys tested at baseline, after a vehicle injection and after klotho; the protein was first checked in mice
18 rhesus monkeys aged 15 to 28 (13 female, 5 male)
one injection under the skin of rhesus klotho protein, 10 µg/kg; 20 and 30 µg/kg tested in an exploratory analysis
memory tests from 4 hours to 2 weeks after the dose
a spatial memory task with easier and harder versions

research.found: At 10 µg/kg, memory scores rose 4 hours after the shot, and the effect lasted at least 2 weeks. The higher doses did not improve memory. The University of California holds a patent on klotho for cognition naming one author as inventor; several authors consulted for or own stock in Unity Biotechnology, and two founded a company to develop klotho therapies.

src.label: Castner et al., Nature Aging, 2023 (full text, PMC)

items.text: mice missing the klotho gene aged early and died young.
mice engineered to overproduce klotho lived longer than normal mice.
in rat pups exposed to high oxygen, klotho injections every other day reduced lung and blood-vessel damage.

research.text: Animal results have not been confirmed in people.

us.text: Not FDA-approved for any use. No klotho product appears in FDA’s drug approval database. Products labelled “research use only” are not for human use. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. A search of Drugs@FDA for klotho found no match.

FDA says products marketed “for research use only” or otherwise not for human consumption “have not been evaluated for safety and should never be used by humans.” Such products may not be sold for human use: FDA says it acts against firms selling unapproved products.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Klotho is not named on the WADA Prohibited List for 2026 or 2027. WADA’s class S0 bans at all times any pharmacological substance not covered elsewhere on the List and with no current approval by any government health regulator for human use. For 2027, WADA adds “peptides” to the examples in S0. The lists do not say whether klotho falls under S0.
Australia: Klotho is not named in the Poisons Standard that took effect on October 1, 2026. The TGA’s product register was not checked.

side.text: There are no human safety data for klotho protein. No published study has given it to people, and the two gene-therapy pilots have posted no results.

items.text: none published. The gene-therapy pilots list side effects as a main measure but have posted no results.
in old monkeys, higher single doses (20 and 30 µg/kg) did not improve memory and did not make it significantly worse. The authors say it is not known whether even higher doses could impair memory.

unconfirmed: UK (MHRA) status and Australia’s TGA register were not checked against the regulator’s own record.
Klotho would be a biological product; FDA’s Purple Book of licensed biologics was not searched, only Drugs@FDA.
The Dubal 2014 abstract gives no number of people for the human genetic analysis; the full paper was not read.
surprises: Klotho is promoted as a longevity protein, but no published study has given klotho protein to a person.
The best-known primate result is from 18 old monkeys given one injection; higher doses did not help, and the authors include a patent inventor and company stockholders.
A klotho gene-therapy pilot is registered with a US testing site, but the registry says the injections are given in Honduras, outside FDA jurisdiction.
